data.text/markdown:
From X-rays to detector counts

Predict an ideal pixel detector's expected counts and compare a seeded Poisson realization.

Define the physical scene

A 30 keV beam illuminates 100 nm HOPG. The 16 × 16 mm panel sits 100 mm away, at 135° from the incident beam direction. Its 16 × 16 pixels have 1 mm pitch. A 0.01 pC bunch at 1 MHz gives 10 nA mean current. These physical beam populations are independent of sampled histories.

Specify what is measured

Geometry belongs to Scene; response and exposure belong to Observation. IdealPhotonCounter() has unit efficiency and no energy broadening. Count photons in the half-open reporting interval [0.5, 4) keV during 1 s. mode="poisson" retains the fractional expectation and adds integer draws. Score 4 × 4 angular tiles across the panel: neighboring pixels share source spectra within each tile, while their pixel-centre ray geometry is retained. Pixel pitch alone does not set the angular scoring resolution.

Interpret and explore

Both images already integrate energy and pixel solid angle, apply the ideal response, and scale by physical electrons during the exposure. Do not multiply by current, solid angle or exposure again. They include PXR/CBS, bremsstrahlung and characteristic emission in the reporting window; underflow, overflow and below-threshold expectations remain separate. No downstream filter or background is included. The nearly uniform expectation and noisier integer image share one color scale. Counting fluctuations are conditional on the estimated source: they exclude its Monte Carlo uncertainty, calibration errors and backgrounds. The modest histories, two reflection families and coarse angular tiles are illustrative; they do not establish convergence or detector calibration. First change only acquisition.seed: the expectation stays fixed while counts change. Then double exposure_s: expected counts double, while the realized total need not double exactly. More source histories refine the expectation; they do not increase the physical exposure. Consult the detector how-to, observation reference, response physics, and validation status.
